newsitem.title: UK: EURO OIL SWAPS DIP ON IRAQ SALES, MOGAS DOWN $5.
newsitem.headline: EURO OIL SWAPS DIP ON IRAQ SALES, MOGAS DOWN $5.

text.p: European oil swaps fell on Friday, led by gasoline which was weak for the third day in a row, losing $5 a tonne on August swaps.
Brent futures sank on news that Iraq had been given the green light to resume oil exports.
A squeeze on gasoline that lifted prices by some $25 a tonne over the past week appeared to have ended on Friday, although some there was some support for the market in late trading.
August swaps were heard traded at $211 compared to a peak of $223.50 on Tuesday while September traded three times at $194.
Physical barges traded at $216 early and later at $22 for very prompt loading but some dealers expected further falls in the wake of the summer driving season.
Naphtha also fell but less sharply as Asian swaps sank further into contango with August dipping $4 to $190.00 and September around $185.50 by the close.
Gas oil was little changed with premiums for EN590 holding around $6 a tonne above the IPE for September and $9.50 above for the fourth quarter.
Heavy fuel was little changed. August traded at $94.50 with September 50 cents higher and the fourth quarter around $96.75.

Brent crude CFDs slipped and sank into deeper contango. Next week's dates fell five cents to 38 cents under October while the following two weeks were down three cents to 34 cents under and 33 cents under respectively.
